systems.reason: Body triangle is its own superior control and has its own retention card ('Body Triangle Squeeze'). A success here should leave you in body triangle; this table drops you to plain back control. Also, with the triangle locked the opponent can't easily turtle, so the failure-to-turtle cell is written for hooks-in back control, not this position.

pragmatist.reason: Body triangle IS back control; keeping the back lands back-control/top, losing it lets them square up to turtle or turn in and end on top in your half guard. All three landings are what actually happens from the triangle.

leg-skeptic.reason: Body triangle is back control with the legs locked; trading the triangle for hooks on success, losing them to turtle on failure, and eating the classic turn-in escape to their top half guard on the counter are all real landings from here.

academic.reason: The body triangle is a back-control variant. Maintenance that resets to hooks-in back control is a real retention habit (you switch to hooks when they start attacking the ankles). An escape to turtle, or their turning into you and coming up on top in half guard, are the real exits. There is no competing body-triangle maintenance card.

gi-fundamentalist.reason: Body triangle is back control with the legs locked: keeping the back lands back-control/top, losing it lets them come to knees under you (turtle/top), and a turn-in leaves you underneath in half guard. All three landings are what I see from here.

guard-back.reason: Body triangle is back control with a different lower-body lock; the seatbelt and hand-fight prose applies directly. Switching the triangle for hooks (success to back-control/top), losing it to a turtle (failure) and the escape to the bottom-leg side ending under top half guard (counter) are all how it really goes from here.

systems.reason: The Z-lock is a knee-shield structure, so retaining the shield from here is the native action. Success into knee-shield half guard, failure flattened in half guard and the same counter all land plausibly, with no drag back to the origin.

pragmatist.reason: The Z shape is a knee shield. Opening the lock into a knee-shield half, or getting flattened when it fails, are exactly where this exchange goes from here. The counter row is as authored at the origin.

leg-skeptic.reason: Z-lock is a knee shield with a lock on it, so letting the lock go and framing the knee is the natural retention move. Success lands knee-shield half, failure gets you flattened, and the counter matches the convention. Coherent from here.

academic.reason: Z-lock is a lockdown and knee-shield hybrid, so switching to knee shield retention is natural. Success into knee shield half, failure flattened out and counter as at the origin are all plausible from here.

gi-fundamentalist.reason: The Z is essentially a knee shield frame, so moving into the knee shield from here is natural. Success into knee shield half guard and failure into flattened half guard (the real danger in any lockdown-style half) are plausible. The counter cell is as suspect as it is at the origin.

guard-back.reason: The Z in Z-lock is a knee shield, so holding it under pressure is a real action from here. Success into plain knee-shield half and failure into flattened half are both plausible. The miss does not drag you into knee-shield half, and the odd counter cell comes with the card, not with listing it here.

gi-guard-modern.reason: Z-lock is a half-guard shield variant, so going to a knee shield and failing into flattened half are the adjacent states. The counter-cell oddity (ending on top) comes from the origin; it is not a new teleport.

unorthodox.reason: From the Z-lock, keeping the top knee as a shield is part of the structure. Success to knee-shield half and failure to flattened half are the honest fork from here.

gi-to-nogi.reason: The Z-lock is built on a knee shield, so sliding into knee-shield half, or being flattened when it fails, is exactly where this exchange goes.

fhl-scrambler.reason: Z-lock is a half-guard variant, so switching into or keeping a knee shield is a natural move from here. Success in knee-shield half and failure to flattened half both land where they would from z-lock half.
